# Stock Git compatibility

Conformance suite **forkmesh-stock-git 1.0.0**. Statuses were computed **2026-09-14** from 2 retained stock-Git runs: **39 of 39** support claims have a passing run from the last 30 days. Supported rows use an unmodified Git executable (minimum 2.34.0); every run records the exact client and platform version in its JSON evidence.

A claim is never published on its own: with no passing run it is **unverified**, when its newest passing run ages past the freshness window it is **stale**, and when a retained run failed it is **failing**. [Filter results by client and workflow](/docs/git-compatibility/) or download [results.json](/docs/git-compatibility/results.json).

The offline reference probe uses disposable repositories and the same smart-HTTP framing as the public read path. Product gateway contract tests cover authorization, hidden refs, read-only failures, and rollback behavior.

Repository shape: A bare repository whose main branch has three commits: an SSH-signed commit adding a README, a 128 KiB binary payload, and a gitlink submodule at deps/fixture resolved through a relative URL, followed by two history commits. A lightweight tag points at the signed commit; receive and transfer fsck are enabled, and a read-only replica rejects every push.

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **supported** | Covered by an automated stock-Git probe and part of the public contract. |
| **local** | Runs in the stock client checkout; the transport preserves the required objects and refs. |
| **conditional** | Supported when the condition in the matrix is satisfied. |
| **unsupported** | Rejected or deliberately unavailable; follow the linked recovery or alternative. |
| **failing** | A retained run for this cell failed; the claim is withdrawn until the same configuration passes again. |
| **stale** | The newest passing run is older than the freshness window; re-run the suite before relying on it. |
| **unverified** | No retained run covers this cell; treat it as experimental. |

## Paths

| Path | Read | Write | Transport | Authentication | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Direct owner SSH | yes | yes | SSH (ssh://); the offline probe uses a stock smart-HTTP origin with the same pack negotiation | Registered SSH public key with repository read or write permission | A stock Git SSH session terminates at the owner-authorized forced-command gateway. |
| Stable relay HTTPS | yes | no | HTTPS smart protocol under the stable repository URL | Anonymous read of a public repository; HTTPS writes are rejected | The stable repository URL proxies upload-pack in place from one integrity-matching HTTPS mirror. |
| Relay mirror failover | yes | no | HTTPS smart protocol through a relay-selected mirror | Anonymous read of a public repository; no credentials reach a mirror | Before response bytes are committed, the relay retries another healthy mirror with the same attested refs. |

## Known limitations

### HTTPS and failover paths are read-only
<a id="https-receive-pack"></a>

- Applies to: relay, mirror-failover.
- Expected result: Git receives HTTP 501 with error code direct_https_receive_pack_required before ForkMesh reads the push body.
- Reproduce: `git push https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY HEAD`
- Action: Register an SSH public key, copy the repository's published ssh:// URL, and push that remote instead.
- Recovery: No remote ref or object is changed. Correct the remote URL and retry the same push.
- Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · app/tests/test_git_http.py::test_receive_pack_fails_closed_without_consuming_request_body

### Repository-controlled server hooks are disabled
<a id="server-hooks"></a>

- Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover.
- Expected result: Client-side hooks in a checkout run normally. Gateways set core.hooksPath to the null device so pushed repository configuration cannot execute code on a mirror.
- Reproduce: `git -C worktree commit -m 'exercise local hook'`
- Action: Keep developer hooks local; put shared required checks in reviewed ForkMesh Actions or another CI system.
- Recovery: A rejected local hook leaves the index and remote unchanged; fix or intentionally bypass the local hook according to project policy.
- Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 hooks probe

### A response cannot change mirrors mid-stream
<a id="midstream-failover"></a>

- Applies to: mirror-failover.
- Expected result: ForkMesh retries another eligible mirror only before response bytes are committed. An interrupted pack fails as a normal Git transport error.
- Reproduce: `git fetch --prune origin`
- Action: Retry the fetch; Git reuses valid local objects and ForkMesh may select another matching mirror for the new request.
- Recovery: Run git fsck --full --strict if the client or disk reported corruption. Do not delete the existing clone before collecting diagnostics.
- Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 mirror-failover and integrity probes

### Partial clone requires Git protocol v2
<a id="partial-protocol-v2"></a>

- Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover.
- Expected result: A protocol-v0 filtered clone may receive the initial commits and trees, but its first lazy blob fetch is rejected as an unadvertised-object request so hidden ForkMesh objects remain inaccessible.
- Reproduce: `git -c protocol.version=0 clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout '{clone_url}' worktree`
- Action: Use Git 2.34 or newer and retry with -c protocol.version=2, or omit --filter for a full clone.
- Recovery: Remove the incomplete disposable clone, or keep it for diagnostics and clone into a new directory with protocol v2; no remote ref or object was changed.
- Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 protocol-v0 rejection and protocol-v2 partial-clone probes

### Submodules are separate repositories
<a id="submodule-authorization"></a>

- Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover.
- Expected result: The superproject clone succeeds, then Git names the exact submodule whose independent URL is unavailable or unauthorized.
- Reproduce: `git clone --recurse-submodules '{clone_url}' worktree`
- Action: Confirm every .gitmodules URL uses a published public HTTPS route or an SSH route your key may read, then run git submodule update --init --recursive.
- Recovery: The superproject and any completed submodules remain valid; Git resumes the missing child without recloning successful repositories.
- Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 submodules probe

### Third-party desktop UI certification is not complete
<a id="desktop-client-validation"></a>

- Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover.
- Expected result: GitHub Desktop, Sourcetree, and GitKraken are not release-supported rows until their exact application and bundled-Git versions produce a retained report.
- Reproduce: `python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --git /path/to/the/client/bundled/git --client-label 'CLIENT VERSION'`
- Action: Use a tested Git CLI or ForkMesh Qt build, or run the versioned probe with the desktop application's bundled Git before relying on it.
- Recovery: The probe uses disposable repositories and makes no production write. Attach its JSON report when requesting a new supported row.
- Last tested: not yet tested · not applicable · No support claim is published without retained evidence.

## Run the suite

```sh
python3 tools/git_conformance.py validate
python3 tools/git_conformance.py render --check
python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 0 \
  --output artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json
python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 2 \
  --output artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json
python3 tools/git_conformance.py attest \
  artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json
python3 tools/git_conformance.py gate
```

Use `--git /path/to/git --client-label 'client version'` to exercise a desktop application's bundled, unmodified Git. Reports contain operation status, elapsed milliseconds, exact client/platform versions, generalized request counts, and test object IDs. They exclude temporary paths, URLs, repository contents, credentials, and client addresses.
